name: Female Infertility Due to Oocyte Meiotic Arrest

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Female Infertility Due to Oocyte Meiotic Arrest

criteria.description: Primary or secondary infertility with failure to conceive after 12 months of unprotected intercourse
Demonstration of oocyte meiotic arrest at metaphase I or prophase I stage via ovarian stimulation and oocyte retrieval
Exclusion of other causes of female infertility such as tubal factor, uterine abnormalities, or hormonal imbalances
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in meiotic progression (e.g., PATL2, TUBB8)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical infertility with confirmed oocyte meiotic arrest and exclusion of other infertility causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated serum FSH and LH
imaging: Normal pelvic ultrasound with normal antral follicle count
No structural abnormalities of uterus or ovaries
other: Oocyte retrieval shows arrested oocytes at metaphase I or prophase I

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated FSH and LH with low AMH
Evidence of tubal blockage or damage on hysterosalpingography
History of pelvic infection or surgery

redFlags: Failure to retrieve mature oocytes after controlled ovarian stimulation
Persistent infertility despite normal ovarian reserve and tubal patency
Genetic mutations affecting meiotic progression identified
references: Zhao et al., 2018. Genetic causes of oocyte meiotic arrest and female infertility. Human Reproduction Update.
Orphanet Report on ORPHA:488191 - Female Infertility Due to Oocyte Meiotic Arrest.
Sun et al., 2020. PATL2 mutations cause female infertility characterized by oocyte meiotic arrest. Journal of Medical Genetics.
